full_judgment: 2. The suit was filed stating, inter alia, that the land recorded in C. S Khatian No. 217 in equal share belonged to Gopinath Gope and Tokani Gope that by amicable partition Gopinath Gope got the land in suit and some other land, that Gopinath Gope died leaving 4 sons and while they were enjoying the property rent fallen in arrear and there upon their land was sold in auction in execution of the decree in Money Suit No. 257 of 1993 and land measuring .11 acre was purchased by Harendra Chandra Bandapadhaya and Sree Upendra Nath  Bandapadhaya and they possessed the same by erecting buildings, that on the basis of amicable partition Sree Upendra Nath Bandapadhaya got the land of plot No. 266 (old) and 297 (Present) and previous plot Nos. 259, 260 and 261 along with other lands and got the revenue record prepared in his name that Sree upendra Nath Bandapadhaya died leaving wife Nagendra Bala Devi, 4 sons by name. Jitendra Nath Rabindra Nath, Dijendra Nath and Bhupendra Nath and they appointed Fazlul Karim and Rafiqul Islam as their Ammoktar by the deed dated March 8, 1959 that of the Said Arnmoktars Rafiqul Islam in exchange of the land of Arndeka Khatun (Asdeka Khatun) in Hugli West Bengal Permanently leased out the land measuring 11 decimals which previously belonged to Upendra Nath Bandapadhaya; by the registered deed dated October 30, 1959 that Amdeka Khatun upon acquiring right, title and interest in the aforesaid manner erected a but and leased out the same., that the land so got by Amdeka Khatun has been recorded in the S. A. record in her name. Amdeka. leased out the land to the defendant No. 1 on monthly rent basis. Defendant No. 1 for some time was the tenant of Amdeka Khatun and thereafter surrendered the possession to her. Amdeka Khatun by the deed executed on June 25, 1977 and registered on August 15, 1977 sold 4 decimals of land of the plot in suit along with some other land for Tk. 10,000/= and made over possession to the plaintiff. Thereafter-defendant No. 1 accepted the plaintiff as owners of the land and took lease of the land at monthly rent of Tk. 100/- on July 16, 1977 and paid rent upto December, 1980. Plaintiff asked the defendant No 1 to vacate the premises but he did not vacate the premises. Thereupon plaintiff served notice on November 9, 1983 under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act terminating monthly tenancy. In reply to the legal notice defendant No. 1 disclosed that his father took lease of .051/) acre of land from Sailendra Chandra Bandapandhaya on payment of 'salami and executing' Amalnarna and receipts were granted by Sailendra Chandra Bandapadhaya. Hence the suit.
